entry.title: From the Runway to the Altar — A Lake Tahoe Wedding

link.title: From the Runway to the Altar — A Lake Tahoe Wedding

entry.content:
There are weddings where everything clicks: the light, the landscape, the couple, the flowers, and Emma and Ross's day in the Sierra Nevada was exactly that.

Their venue sat in the foothills just outside the Lake Tahoe basin, at River Highlands Ranch, and it's the kind of setting that makes your job as a florist feel like a privilege. The property was rich with natural texture: rolling meadows, rugged mountain views, old-growth trees, and that quality of late-afternoon Sierra light that turns everything into gold. It's a setting that doesn't need much embellishment. Our job was simply to respond to it.

The Floral Vision

Emma came to us with a clear sense of what she wanted and we leaned into that fully. The palette drew from classic green and whites and she wanted an edgy, heavy amaranth moment. We worked with seasonal blooms — tulips, star of bethlehem, tweedia, calla lilies, ranunculus and of course the amaranth. Nothing too precious. Everything intentional. Everything was grown in California by farmers we know.

The reception brought everything together. Long tables were dressed with low, meandering centerpieces — not blocking conversation, but drawing the eye down the length of the table and creating that sense of a garden pulled indoors. Tapers and candlelight did the rest.

Designing for the Sierra Nevada

Outdoor mountain weddings have their own set of considerations, and Lake Tahoe area florals need to be built for the environment. Wind and temperature shifts are real, the Sierra Nevada has its own microclimate, and arrangements need to be designed accordingly. We build our florals with longevity in mind: appropriate water sources, sturdy stems, and bloom timing that accounts for mountain conditions.

The natural surroundings are also your greatest asset. Rich earth tones, organic textures, and garden-inspired arrangements always feel more at home in this landscape than something structured or formal. The mountains are the backdrop — the flowers should feel like they grew nearby.

And because we're based right here in Incline Village, we know this land well. We source from California growers, including from our own cutting garden, which means the flowers arriving at your wedding are as fresh and regionally grounded as they can be.

The Team That Made It Happen

Days like Emma and Ross's don't happen without a vendor community that knows how to work together. We were honored to share the floor with:

  • Photography: Nichole Lee Photo

  • Videography: Abel Guitron Photography

  • Hair & Makeup: Polish and Pout

  • Jewelry: Sierra Moon Goldsmiths

  • Cake: Crave Cakes

Every one of these vendors brought craft and intention to Emma and Ross's day, and it showed in every frame.

Planning a Lake Tahoe Mountain Wedding?

If you're engaged and considering a Sierra Nevada or Lake Tahoe area wedding, we'd love to talk. Golden Flowers is a boutique wedding florist based in Incline Village, Nevada, designing foam-free, locally sourced florals for mountain weddings across the Tahoe basin and beyond.

We take on a limited number of weddings each season so that every one gets our full attention. If your date is still open, reach out here — we'd love to hear about your vision.

entry.title: The Science of Sierra Florals. Why an Agronomist Designs the Best Lake Tahoe Wedding Flowers

link.title: The Science of Sierra Florals. Why an Agronomist Designs the Best Lake Tahoe Wedding Flowers

entry.content:
If you have spent any time scrolling through wedding inspiration online, you have likely saved photos of lush, pillowy peonies, delicate sweet peas, and dramatic, texture-heavy dahlias. But there is a massive gap between a beautiful digital photo and the reality of making those same blooms look flawless on a sun-drenched pier in Incline Village or a granite ridge at Martis Camp.

Most florists treat flowers as inventory: bundles shipped in cardboard boxes from international brokers.

We view them through a completely different lens. Before founding Golden Florals, my background was rooted in science. With a Master’s degree in agricultural science and a decade-long career as a corporate agronomist helping operations like Whole Foods Market align consumer desires with sustainable growing practices, I look at your Lake Tahoe wedding flowers from the roots up.

Here is why working with an agronomist-backed Lake Tahoe wedding florist completely transforms the look, longevity, and impact of your wedding day design.

1. The "Grown, Not Flown" Difference

When flowers are flown in from across the globe, they are cut entirely too early, treated with heavy synthetic preservatives, and stripped of their natural vitality. By the time they arrive at your venue, they are running on empty.

Because we operate our own flower farm plots right here in the Sierra Nevada foothills, your wedding flowers are harvested at the absolute peak of their natural life cycle. What we don't grow ourselves, we source directly from trusted local California growers whom I know personally.

When a stem goes from California soil to your bridal bouquet in a matter of days, rather than weeks in a cargo hold, it carries a distinct brilliance. The colors are richer, the petals are sturdier, and the texture has a living, breathing movement that imports simply cannot replicate.

2. Navigating Tahoe’s Microclimates Month-by-Month

Lake Tahoe’s high-altitude growing season is fast, dramatic, and spectacular. Sourcing the right florals requires knowing exactly what the California landscape is naturally offering during the specific week of your wedding.

  • Early Summer (May and June): This is the magic window for our farm-grown peonies, romantic ranunculus, and fragrant sweet peas. They thrive in the bright, cool early-season mountain air.

  • Late Summer & Early Fall (August – October): This is when the landscape shifts to rich texture. Our plots explode with architectural amaranth, velvety celosia, and heavy, dramatic dahlias that perfectly mirror the changing golden light over the lake.

By aligning your design with the natural rhythms of the season, your florals won't just survive the mountain elements, they will look like they truly belong to the landscape.

3. Merging Scientific Mechanics with High-End Art

Designing luxury installations without the use of toxic, microplastic floral foam isn't just an environmental choice—it's a structural challenge.

Our foam-free approach relies heavily on agricultural resourcefulness. We engineer custom, weighted structures and utilize natural tension to hold stems securely, ensuring your centerpieces and arches stay perfectly hydrated and structurally sound against unexpected alpine gusts. The result? Florals that flow with organic grace, grounded in texture and movement rather than rigid, geometric formulas.

4. Undivided Focus for a Flawless Execution

Because mountain logistics require strict attention to detail, we deliberately accept only one wedding per date.

We don't split our harvests, our design team, or our focus. When you book with us, my background in agricultural logistics is entirely at your disposal. From analyzing how the shifting sun at Edgewood Tahoe or The Ritz-Carlton will hit your ceremony space to executing complex, foam-free installations on-site, your day gets our complete, uninterrupted dedication.

Let’s Create Something Alive

Your wedding flowers should be more than just a centerpiece decoration—they should be a living extension of the wild, breathtaking beauty of the Sierra Nevada.

If you are ready to move past formulaic arrangements and embrace intentional, artful design rooted in the land, we would love to guide you. Explore our Full-Service Design Experience to begin planning your Tahoe celebration.

entry.title: From Lakeside to Mountain Peaks. Designing Resilient, Elevated Lake Tahoe Wedding Flowers

link.title: From Lakeside to Mountain Peaks. Designing Resilient, Elevated Lake Tahoe Wedding Flowers

entry.content:
For couples planning a destination wedding in the Sierra Nevada, the draw is undeniable. The crystal-clear alpine water, the towering pines, and the dramatic granite backdrops. But designing a luxury wedding in an alpine environment requires more than just an eye for aesthetics, it requires a deep, scientific understanding of how nature behaves at 6,000+ feet.

When you are planning your Lake Tahoe wedding flowers, you aren't just choosing a color palette; you are choosing living elements that must thrive in intense high-altitude sun, sudden alpine breezes, and shifting mountain microclimates.

As a premier Lake Tahoe wedding florist, our design philosophy bridges the gap between high-end, intentional art and the realities of the natural landscape. Here is how we design elevated, sustainable florals that look flawless from your lakeside ceremony to your mountaintop reception.

1. Designing for the High-Altitude Climate

The alpine sun is spectacular, but it is also incredibly drying. Imported flowers that have spent days in cargo planes simply cannot handle the transition to Tahoe’s high altitude; they wilt before the cocktail hour even begins.

To combat this, we approach your florals from a grower’s perspective. Because our flowers are harvested fresh from our local Sierra Nevada foothill farm plots and trusted California growers, they are naturally adapted to the climate. Varieties like local peonies, resilient garden roses, textured dahlias, and architectural amaranth possess the cellular structure to stay vibrant and crisp throughout a long, sunny afternoon at venues like Edgewood Tahoe or The Chateau at Incline Village.

2. The Art of the Wind-Resistant, Foam-Free Installation

Whether you are saying your vows on the water's edge at the Hellman-Ehrman Mansion or high up the mountain at Palisades High Camp, Tahoe is known for its afternoon breezes. Traditional florists rely heavily on green floral foam to hold arrangements in place—a microplastic that is not only toxic to Tahoe’s fragile waterways but also creates rigid, stiff arrangements that can catch the wind like a sail.

We choose a different path. We design 100% foam-free. By engineering custom, weighted mechanics and utilizing organic, nested structures, your lake tahoe wedding flowers are allowed to move naturally with the wind rather than fight it. This organic movement creates that sought-after, quietly elevated aesthetic where your ceremony arch feels like it naturally grew out of the Sierra landscape, completely safe and structurally sound.

3. Transitioning Florals Across Multi-Space Venues

Many of the finest Tahoe venues offer a multi-experience layout. You might have a ceremony on a sun-drenched lakeside lawn, followed by an indoor ballroom reception at The Ritz-Carlton, Lake Tahoe.

Achieving a cohesive design means ensuring your florals transition seamlessly between these vastly different spaces. A truly intentional design considers how the changing mountain light will affect your color palette.

  • In the bright, direct alpine sun: Pale pastels can sometimes look washed out, while deep, saturated tones or highly textured neutrals hold their ground beautifully.

  • For the indoor reception: We design statement pieces—like lush, foam-free column installations and delicate bud vases—that bring the wild, effortless texture of the mountains inside, creating an intimate environment for your guests.

4. Working with a Single-Focus Florist

Because the logistics of navigating mountain passes, shifting weather patterns, and meticulous venue timelines require absolute precision, execution is everything.

When interviewing a Lake Tahoe wedding florist, always ask about their capacity. At Golden Florals, we consciously limit our calendar to take only one wedding per date. This intentional approach ensures that our entire creative team, our logistics crew, and our freshest farm harvests are dedicated exclusively to your day. From the first morning delivery to the final late-night strike, your wedding gets our undivided focus.

Let’s Build Something Built to Belong

Your wedding florals shouldn't look like they could have existed anywhere else. They should be a reflection of the season, the local soil, and the stunning geography of the Sierra Nevada.

If you are ready to design intentional, breathtaking flowers for your Lake Tahoe celebration, we invite you to connect with us. Explore our Full-Service Design Experience and schedule a consultation.

entry.title: Sustainable Lake Tahoe Wedding Flowers: Why Foam-Free Design Matters for Your Sierra Celebration

link.title: Sustainable Lake Tahoe Wedding Flowers: Why Foam-Free Design Matters for Your Sierra Celebration

entry.content:
When you picture your Lake Tahoe wedding, you likely imagine the crisp mountain air, the towering pines, and the crystal-clear water. The natural beauty of the Sierra Nevada is exactly why couples travel from all over the world to marry here.

But traditional wedding floristry holds a dirty secret: microplastics and massive carbon footprints from flying flowers across the globe.

Choosing sustainable, California-grown, and foam-free wedding flowers ensures your celebration honors the landscape instead of harming it.

TL;DR: WHAT MAKES WEDDING FLORALS SUSTAINABLE? • Foam-Free Mechanics: Eliminating toxic, non-biodegradable floral foam. • Hyper-Local Sourcing: Using flowers grown right here in the Sierra foothills. • Seasonal Integrity: Designing with what nature naturally offers during your wedding month.

The Hidden Environmental Impact of Traditional Wedding Florals

Most people don't realize that standard floral arrangements rely heavily on green "floral foam" to hold stems in place.

What is floral foam? It is a petroleum-based plastic that does not dissolve. Instead, it breaks down into toxic microplastics that leach into local water systems. For a delicate ecosystem like the Lake Tahoe Basin or the Yuba River watershed in Nevada City, this waste is incredibly harmful.

Furthermore, shipping flowers from South America or Europe burns massive amounts of jet fuel and requires heavy chemical preservatives just to keep the blooms alive during transit.

The Sustainable Alternative: Grown, Not Flown

Choosing a sustainable florist means looking at the logistics of how your flowers get to your venue. True sustainability relies on three main pillars:

1. Foam-Free Design Mechanics

Modern, eco-conscious floral design utilizes reusable metal grids, chicken wire, and water vials. These artisanal techniques require more skill and structural engineering, but they create a look that feels alive, full of movement, and organically draped—rather than stiff and manufactured.

2. Sourcing from Local Soil

By utilizing flowers grown on small Sierra Nevada foothill farms and sourcing exclusively from trusted California growers, your flowers are harvested at their peak. They don’t spend a week in a cardboard box on an airplane; they travel just a few miles from the field to your reception desk.

3. Embracing the Rhythms of the Season

When you let the season dictate your palette, magic happens. From spring ranunculus and sweet peas to late-summer dahlias and autumn amaranth, seasonal flowers naturally belong in the local mountain light.

Seasonal Flower Guide for Sierra Nevada & Tahoe Weddings

To help you map out your wedding style, here is a quick look at what blooms naturally thrive in our local California soil across different seasons:

Wedding Season Best Local Blooms available in California

Spring Peonies, Ranunculus, Sweet Peas, Tulips. Great for soft, romantic, delicate textures

Summer Dahlias, Zinnias, Cosmos, Celosia. Great for vibrant, bold, wildflower movement

Fall Amaranth, Heirloom Garden Roses, Grasses, Foraged Foliage. Great for warm, earthy, deeply textured, moody

Winter Evergreens, branches, cones, berries, poinsettias. Great for warm, earthy, modern

Why An Agronomist’s Approach Changes Everything

"True artful floral design is a collaborative conversation between your wedding vision and the local landscape."

At Golden Flowers, our approach is deeply rooted in science. Founded by Brittany—an agronomist with a Master’s degree in Agricultural Science and formal training in European floral design—we approach arrangements from a grower's perspective.

Because we manage our own farm plots in the Sierra Nevada foothills, we understand the specific water, soil, and temperature needs of every single stem. We don't build formulaic arrangements; we build installations that feel like they naturally grew right where you are getting married.

Whether we are designing a luxury installation at the Ritz-Carlton Lake Tahoe, a lakeside ceremony at Valhalla, or an intimate, historic gathering at the National Exchange Hotel in Nevada City, we design to complement the unique architecture and natural light of your venue.

Ready to Design Your Sustainable Sierra Wedding?

If you want your wedding day to be elevated, elegant, and entirely respectful of the environment, we would love to help bring your vision to life. We offer full-service floral design across the Lake Tahoe Basin, Truckee, Incline Village, and Nevada County.

  • Step 1: Check out our Full-Service Gallery to see our past work.

  • Step 2: Contact our studio to check availability for your date.

Frequently Asked Questions About Eco-Friendly Florals

Does sustainable floral design limit my color choices?

Not at all. California has incredibly diverse microclimates allowing for a massive spectrum of colors year-round. By using local flowers, your colors will look richer and more vibrant because the blooms are completely fresh, not chemically treated.

Is a foam-free installation secure for outdoor Tahoe wind?

Yes. Using advanced mechanics like weighted metal bases, custom brackets, and hidden water delivery systems, foam-free structures are incredibly heavy and secure. They easily withstand the afternoon mountain breezes at high-altitude venues like Palisades High Camp or Edgewood.

How far in advance should I book my wedding florist?

Because we limit our calendar to ensure every couple gets our undivided attention and the best harvest from our farm plots, we recommend reaching out 6 to 8 months before your wedding date once your venue is locked in.

Published by the team at Golden Flowers. Specializing in sustainable, artful floral design for Lake Tahoe weddings.

entry.title: How to DIY Your Wedding Flowers: The Ultimate Step-by-Step Guide for Creative Couples

link.title: How to DIY Your Wedding Flowers: The Ultimate Step-by-Step Guide for Creative Couples

entry.content:
There is something incredibly romantic about the idea of designing your own wedding flowers. Hand-selecting your blooms, spending the morning before your wedding with your bridal party surrounded by fresh stems, and seeing your personal touch all over your venue is deeply rewarding.

However, as a flower grower and professional floral designer based in Lake Tahoe, I’ll be the first to tell you: DIY wedding flowers are a major logistical undertaking. If you are organized, have a great support team, and love a creative project, it is entirely possible. To help you pull it off beautifully and sustainably, here is the ultimate insider guide to DIYing your wedding flowers without the wedding-week panic.

THE GOLDEN RULES OF DIY FLORALS:
• Keep it simple: Stick to bud vases and simple bouquets; leave heavy arches to pros.
• Over-order by 10-15%: Account for broken heads or stems damaged in transit.
• Ditch the foam: Use sustainable, eco-friendly mechanics to keep your flowers alive.

Step 1: Evaluate Your Timeline and Venue Logistics

Before you buy a single stem, look at the clock. Flowers are perishable, living things. You cannot design them weeks in advance.

A realistic DIY floral timeline looks like this:

  • 2-3 Days Before: Pick up or receive your wholesale/farm flowers. Process them (cut stems, strip lower leaves) and hydrate them in clean buckets in a cool, dark space.

  • 1 Day Before: Assemble bouquets, centerpieces, and boutonnières. This easily takes 6 to 10 hours depending on your guest count.

  • Wedding Day: Transport the arrangements to the venue, set them up, and place them in water.

⚠️ Pro-Tip: Do you have a refrigerated space or a very cool, dark garage? High-altitude mountain air in Lake Tahoe or summer heat will wilt unprotected flowers fast.

Step 2: How to Calculate Your Flower Stem Count

The biggest mistake DIY couples make is under-ordering. To figure out how many flowers you actually need, use this simple formula matrix:

Multiply these numbers by your total table/bouquet count, and then add 10% to your final order as a safety net.

Step 3: Source Your Flowers Sustainably (Grown, Not Flown)

Instead of ordering cheap, chemically preserved flowers online that have been flown across the world, look for hyper-local sources.

If you are getting married in Northern California, you are in luck. Sourcing your DIY flowers from local Sierra foothill flower farms or California flower markets ensures your blooms are incredibly fresh, structurally strong, and haven't spent days choking in a shipping box. Fresh, locally harvested flowers are far more forgiving for beginners because their stems are naturally resilient. FloraFresh in Sacramento is a flower wholesaler that is open to the public and carries products grown by local farmers.

Step 4: Master Foam-Free DIY Mechanics

Traditional florists often use green floral foam to hold arrangements in place. As an agronomist, I highly recommend avoiding it. Not only is it a petroleum-based microplastic that harms our local Sierra watersheds, but it can actually restrict water intake if a beginner doesn't prep it perfectly.

Instead, use these easy, sustainable DIY alternatives:

  • The Chicken Wire Method: Crumple a small piece of coated chicken wire into a ball and fit it tightly inside your vase. It creates a perfect structural grid that holds your flower stems exactly where you want them.

  • The Waterproof Tape Grid: For wide-mouthed clear vases, use clear waterproof floral tape to create a tic-tac-toe grid across the top of the opening. Drop your stems into the squares to keep them upright.

  • Bud Vases: If you are nervous about design, stick entirely to bud vases. Grouping 3 to 5 small vases with just 2 or 3 stems each down the center of a long table looks effortlessly elegant, modern, and takes a fraction of the time to build.

Step 5: Processing and Designing Like a Pro

When your flowers arrive, they will look tired. Don't panic! They just need a drink.

  1. Clean Your Buckets: Use soap and bleach. Bacteria is the #1 killer of cut flowers.

  2. Strip the Leaves: Remove any foliage that will sit below the water line in your buckets or vases. Leaves left in water will rot and create bacteria.

  3. Give a Fresh Cut: Cut every stem at a 45-degree angle under running water or right before dropping it into the bucket.

  4. Let Them Rest: Give your flowers at least 12–24 hours to "drink up" in a cool place before you start designing them.

When to DIY vs. When to Hire a Professional

We love DIY couples, but we also know the exact moment the stress tends to set in. If you want a hybrid approach to save room in your budget, here is a great rule of thumb:

  • Perfect for DIY: Tablescapes, bud vases, simple greenery runners, and bridesmaid bouquets.

  • Leave to a Professional: Large ceremony arches, hanging installations, heavy floral mantels, and complex bridal bouquets.

Large-scale installations require architectural engineering, wind-proofing (especially for outdoor Lake Tahoe weddings), and specialized hydration mechanics that are incredibly difficult to manage on the morning of your own wedding.

DIY Wedding Flower FAQs

Can I collect wild flowers from around Lake Tahoe for my wedding?

No. Foraging on public lands or state parks in the Sierra Nevada region is illegal without specific permits, and many local alpine wildflowers are protected species. Always source from local farms or licensed wholesalers to protect our local ecosystem.

What tools do I absolutely need for DIY florals?

You only need three essentials: professional floral shears (don't use regular kitchen scissors, they crush the stems), waterproof floral tape, and plenty of clean 5-gallon buckets.

How do I transport DIY flowers to my venue safely?

Place your finished centerpieces and bouquets inside shallow cardboard boxes (like wine boxes) packed tightly together so they cannot tip over in your car. Turn the vehicle's air conditioning on high, never transport flowers in a hot trunk!

Sound like too much work?

Hire our team to handle it for you. Reach out to our studio today to check availability for your date!

entry.title: Principles of High-End, Organic Floral Design. The Art of Effortless Beauty.

link.title: Principles of High-End, Organic Floral Design. The Art of Effortless Beauty.

entry.content:
There is a common misconception that luxury floral design is simply about sourcing the most expensive stems and grouping them together. But if you have ever looked at a centerpiece and felt like it looked "stiff" or "crowded," you have seen what happens when design principles are ignored.

Truly elevated floral design isn't accidental. It relies on foundational principles of art—form, color theory, texture, and space—to create arrangements that feel alive, intentional, and balanced.

When we design lake tahoe wedding flowers, our goal is never to force nature into a rigid, geometric shape. Instead, we use the fundamentals of organic design to mirror the wild, effortless beauty of the Sierra Nevada.

If you are currently gathering inspiration for your day, here is a look behind the curtain at the design fundamentals an expert Lake Tahoe wedding florist uses to bring a vision to life.

1. Establishing Form: The Skeleton of the Design

Every arrangement begins with "line flowers" and structural branches that establish the overall shape and boundary of the piece. In traditional design, this might mean a perfectly symmetrical pyramid or sphere. In high-end, organic design, we look for asymmetric, sweeping forms.

We look for branches that have a natural bend, or vines that reach outward. This creates a sense of growth and mimics how flowers actually look in a garden or a mountain meadow. By establishing an organic form first, the final installation feels like an extension of the venue itself, whether it's framing an outdoor lakeside ceremony or softening an indoor ballroom.

2. Layering Texture Over Tradition

Texture is the secret ingredient that transforms a flat arrangement into a multi-dimensional masterpiece. A bouquet made entirely of tightly packed roses lacks depth because the eye has nowhere to rest.

To create depth, we layer three distinct types of materials:

  • Focal Blooms: Large, pillowy flowers like garden roses, dahlias, or peonies that draw the initial gaze.

  • Secondary Textures: Ruffled sweet peas, delicate scabiosa, or architectural seed pods that add complexity.

  • Air Flowers: Wispy, delicate stems like astilbe or local grasses that sit just above the rest of the arrangement, catching the light and the mountain breeze.

3. Creating Movement and Negative Space

One of the most critical fundamentals of floral design is actually what you don't see: negative space. High-end arrangements need room to breathe. When flowers are crammed too tightly together, their individual beauty is lost, and the arrangement loses its sense of life.

By leaving deliberate pockets of space within a centerpiece or an arch, we allow individual stems to dance. This creates movement. When your guests sit down at their tables, their eyes should naturally travel through the arrangement, discovering different hidden details, textures, and color gradients from every angle.

4. Color Storytelling, Not Just Color Matching

A fundamental rule of sophisticated palette design is avoiding "matchy-matchy" colors. If your bridesmaid dresses are dusty blue, filling your bouquets with dyed blue flowers often looks unnatural and dated.

Instead, we design using a shifting color story. We pull the underlying undertones from your palette, perhaps using soft peach, creamy ivory, and rich, textured sage green to make that dusty blue pop naturally. Because our flowers are harvested fresh from our foothill farm plots and local California growers, they possess natural, subtle color variations that synthetic imports simply cannot replicate.

Trusting the Process

Understanding these fundamentals is why our team limits our calendar to only one wedding per date. Creating movement, balancing negative space, and building complex, foam-free mechanics on-site requires time, patience, and absolute focus.

When you hire a designer who honors the science and art of floral fundamentals, you aren't just getting centerpieces—you are getting a cohesive, living atmosphere tailored exclusively to your love story. entry.title: Wedding Flowers at Edgewood Tahoe, What Couples Need to Know

link.title: Wedding Flowers at Edgewood Tahoe, What Couples Need to Know

entry.content:
There are Lake Tahoe wedding venues, and then there's Edgewood Tahoe.

The ceremony lawn stretches down to the water's edge with an unobstructed view across the lake to the Nevada mountains. The reception spaces balance rustic warmth with genuine luxury. The light, especially in late afternoon when the sun drops behind the ridgeline and turns everything gold, is unlike anywhere else on the lake.

Designing wedding flowers at Edgewood Tahoe is one of our favorite things we do. Here's what couples planning an Edgewood wedding should know about getting the florals right.

The venue does a lot of the work your flowers need to honor that

Edgewood's setting is so powerful that the worst thing you can do with flowers is fight it. Overly formal, tightly structured arrangements look out of place against the natural grandeur of the lake and the Sierra Nevada skyline. The couples whose Edgewood weddings we've loved most have chosen florals that feel like they belong in that landscape: organic, textural, grounded in the season, with movement and life rather than symmetry and stiffness.

At Golden Flowers we design foam-free, seasonally sourced Lake Tahoe wedding flowers that are built specifically around the venue and the season. At Edgewood, that typically means leaning into what the Sierra Nevada is actually offering on your wedding date, dahlias and garden roses in summer, deep burgundy and rust tones in fall, lush greenery and ranunculus in early season, rather than importing stems that have nothing to do with the place.

Ceremony florals at Edgewood Tahoe

The ceremony lawn at Edgewood is the signature moment and the backdrop of Lake Tahoe makes every photo extraordinary. The floral installation here needs to be significant enough to read against that view without competing with it.

What works well at Edgewood ceremonies:

Asymmetric arches — a single arch with abundant, asymmetrically placed florals reads beautifully against the lake view and photographs better than a perfectly balanced structure. The organic asymmetry echoes the natural landscape.

Ground installations — floral arrangements placed at ground level flanking the ceremony space add depth and texture without blocking sightlines to the water.

Aisle markers — at Edgewood the aisle itself is a feature. Low, lush aisle markers in seasonal blooms guide the eye toward the ceremony arch and the lake beyond.

Petal aisles — a simple but effective addition that photographs beautifully and adds scent to the ceremony space.

Reception florals at Edgewood Tahoe

Edgewood's reception spaces the Edgewood Ballroom and the outdoor terrace have their own character. The ballroom has warm wood tones and a refined aesthetic that responds well to lush, abundant table arrangements with height variation. It is also undergoing a massive renovation. The terrace, open to the lake view, calls for something more relaxed and organic.

For table arrangements at Edgewood we typically recommend:

Low, abundant centerpieces for outdoor or view-facing tables, you don't want floral height blocking the lake. Lush, garden-style arrangements that spill slightly over their vessels look natural and abundant without being formal.

For indoor reception spaces, height variation across the room creates drama and visual interest. A mix of taller arrangements on some tables and lower, spreading arrangements on others gives the room movement and prevents the flat uniformity that makes a reception space feel ordinary.

What's in season for your Edgewood wedding date

One of the advantages of working with a locally rooted Lake Tahoe wedding florist for your Edgewood wedding is access to what's genuinely in season. Here's a rough guide:

June — ranunculus, sweet peas, local peonies, early dahlias, clematis. Soft and romantic, perfect for the fresh Sierra spring light.

July & August — peak dahlia season, garden roses, lisianthus, locally grown sunflowers. The most abundant and varied palette of the year.

September & October — our favorite months at Edgewood. The autumn light on the lake is extraordinary, and the seasonal palette, deep dahlias, amaranth, autumn foliage produces some of the most dramatic and beautiful wedding flowers we design all year.

Logistics couples should know

Edgewood has specific vendor requirements and setup windows that affect floral installation. As a florist who has worked at Edgewood Tahoe, we know the load-in process, the timing, and what the venue's coordination team expects. That experience matters on a wedding day you don't want your florist navigating vendor logistics for the first time on your wedding morning.

When interviewing florists for an Edgewood wedding, ask specifically whether they have experience at the venue. The answer will tell you a lot.

Booking your Edgewood Tahoe wedding florist

Edgewood is one of Lake Tahoe's most sought-after wedding venues and the most sought-after dates fill fast. Florists who work at Edgewood regularly follow the same pattern. If you have an Edgewood date, reaching out to your florist early: 12–18 months in advance for peak season dates, which gives you the best selection and the most time to develop a design that truly does the venue justice.

Golden Flowers has designed Lake Tahoe wedding flowers at Edgewood Tahoe and across the Lake Tahoe basin. We take one wedding per date, work entirely foam-free, and source seasonally from California growers and our own farm plots in the Sierra Nevada foothills.

If you're planning a wedding at Edgewood Tahoe, we'd love to hear about it.

entry.title: Planning a Lake Tahoe Wedding from Sacramento: Finding Your Wedding Florist

link.title: Planning a Lake Tahoe Wedding from Sacramento: Finding Your Wedding Florist

entry.content:
Sacramento couples have a distinct advantage when planning a Lake Tahoe wedding that couples flying in from Los Angeles or New York simply don't have: you're two hours away. Close enough to visit your venues in person, close enough to meet your vendors face to face, and close enough to truly understand what Lake Tahoe looks and feels like in the season you're getting married.

That proximity changes how you plan and it changes what you should expect from your Lake Tahoe wedding florist.

You can actually visit

Most destination wedding couples plan entirely remotely. Sacramento couples can drive up on a Saturday morning, walk through their venue, meet their florist in the studio, and be home for dinner. That's a meaningful advantage when you're making decisions about something as tactile and visual as flowers.

If you're a Sacramento couple planning a Lake Tahoe wedding, take advantage of it. Schedule a studio visit with your florist. See the flowers in person. Walk your venue with them if you can. The design process is better when it's grounded in a real place rather than mood boards and screens.

Golden Flowers is based in Incline Village on the Nevada side of Lake Tahoe, about two hours from Sacramento via Highway 50. We welcome studio visits by appointment and are happy to walk venues with couples who want to think through the design in context.

What's growing when Sacramento couples typically get married

Sacramento couples tend to get married at Lake Tahoe in summer and early fall — June through October — which happens to be the most spectacular growing season in the Sierra Nevada. Here's what's available by month:

June — ranunculus, sweet peas, early dahlias, local peonies, clematis. The Sierra spring arrives late and produces some of the most beautiful blooms of the year. June Lake Tahoe weddings have a softness and freshness that's hard to replicate later in the season.

July & August — peak season for dahlias, garden roses, lisianthus, sunflowers, and an abundance of locally grown seasonal stems. The light at this time of year, long golden evenings, the lake shimmering below, is what most couples picture when they imagine a Lake Tahoe wedding.

September & October — our personal favorite. Deep dahlias in burgundy, rust, and plum. Amaranth. Autumn foliage from the Sierra Nevada hillsides woven through arrangements. The light turns golden and the crowds thin out. Fall Lake Tahoe weddings are genuinely underrated and Sacramento couples who choose this window often get the best of everything, better availability, better rates, and florals that feel perfectly matched to the season.

The two-hour factor works both ways

Being close to Lake Tahoe is an advantage, but it also means Sacramento couples sometimes underestimate booking timelines. Because it feels accessible, there's a temptation to plan on a shorter timeline than a couple flying in from New York would.

Don't. Peak season Lake Tahoe wedding florists, especially those who take one wedding per date like Golden Flowers, book 12–18 months out for June through October dates.

If you have a date and a venue, your florist should be one of the first calls you make. The rest of your planning will be easier once your key creative vendors are locked in.

What to look for in a Lake Tahoe wedding florist as a Sacramento couple

Because you can visit in person, you have the ability to evaluate florists more thoroughly than most destination couples. Here's what's worth looking for:

Local sourcing. A florist who grows their own flowers or sources from California growers will produce fresher, more seasonal, more site-specific arrangements than one importing stems from across the country. Ask specifically where their flowers come from.

Foam-free design. Floral foam is increasingly outdated, it's harmful to waterways and actually produces less natural-looking arrangements than foam-free mechanics. Golden Flowers has always designed foam-free. If you care about sustainability, ask your florist about this directly.

Venue experience. Lake Tahoe venues vary enormously, from lakeside resorts at elevation to granite mountaintop ceremony sites. A florist who has worked at your specific venue understands the logistics, the light, and the installation requirements in a way a newcomer doesn't. Ask who they've worked with.

Single-wedding dates. Some florists book multiple weddings on the same day. That means split attention, split sourcing, and split team capacity. Golden Flowers takes one wedding per date. Always. It's worth asking.

A note on the drive

Highway 50 from Sacramento to South Lake Tahoe is one of the great Sierra Nevada drives especially in summer and fall when the canyon is green and the light filters through the pines. Highway 267 from Truckee to Kings Beach or the Mount Rose Highway from Reno to Incline Village are alternatives depending on your venue location.

If you're planning a studio visit or venue walkthrough, we're happy to suggest the best route based on where you're coming from and where your venue is located.

We'd love to work with you

Golden Flowers has worked with many Sacramento couples planning Lake Tahoe destination weddings: at Edgewood Tahoe, the Ritz-Carlton at Northstar, Palisades High Camp, the Hellman-Ehrman Mansion, and private estates across the basin.

If you're a Sacramento couple planning a Lake Tahoe wedding, reach out early. Summer and fall dates fill fast and we take one wedding per date — which means when we're booked, we're booked.

entry.title: Fall Wedding Flowers at Lake Tahoe. What’s in Season and Why It’s the Best Time of Year

link.title: Fall Wedding Flowers at Lake Tahoe. What’s in Season and Why It’s the Best Time of Year

entry.content:
Ask any Lake Tahoe wedding florist what their favorite time of year is and most will say the same thing without hesitating: fall.

September and October at Lake Tahoe are something else entirely. The summer crowds thin out. The light turns amber and long. The lake goes from its summer blue-green to something deeper and more dramatic. The hillsides start to shift, aspens going gold, shrubs turning rust and burgundy at the edges. And the flowers that are in season at that time of year are, in our opinion, the most beautiful of the entire calendar.

If you're considering a fall Lake Tahoe wedding and wondering what your flowers could look like, here's everything you need to know.

What's actually in season in fall at Lake Tahoe

The Sierra Nevada growing season runs later than most couples expect. Because of the altitude, the season that would be "summer" at lower elevations is still actively producing through September and well into October in the foothills. That means fall Lake Tahoe wedding flowers are genuinely abundant, not a compromise.

Dahlias are the signature fall bloom and they peak in September and October. At this time of year you get the deepest, most dramatic colors: cafe au lait, burgundy, deep plum, burnt orange, blush, and white. Dahlias are also one of the few flowers that look better in organic, foam-free arrangements than in tightly structured ones, which makes them a natural fit for our design style.

Amaranth — the cascading, velvet-textured burgundy or green stems that drape beautifully from arrangements and ceremony arches. Amaranth is almost exclusively a fall bloom and it adds movement and drama that no other flower quite replicates.

Cosmos — delicate, airy, and abundant in fall. They add lightness to arrangements that could otherwise feel heavy with the deeper tones of the season.

Marigolds — used thoughtfully rather than as a primary bloom, marigolds add warmth and a distinctly autumnal quality to fall arrangements. Their scent is also remarkable.

Autumn foliage — not flowers, but equally important. Sierra Nevada foliage in September and October: turning aspens, smoke bush, cotinus, and locally gathered branches gives fall Lake Tahoe wedding flowers a texture and depth that purely floral arrangements can't achieve. We forage locally and incorporate what the landscape is offering on your specific wedding date.

Seasonal grasses and seed heads — bunny tail grass and dried seed pods add texture, movement, and a sense of place that feels completely natural in a Sierra Nevada setting.

The fall Lake Tahoe palette

Fall Lake Tahoe wedding flowers tend to fall into a few natural palettes that work beautifully with the season and the landscape:

Warm and earthy — cafe au lait dahlias, burnt orange, rust, terracotta, deep burgundy, warm white. Feels grounded and autumnal without being Halloween. This palette photographs extraordinarily well in fall light.

Deep and romantic — deep plum, burgundy, dusty rose, blush, and ivory. Moody and luxe, particularly beautiful for evening receptions when candlelight picks up the depth of the colors.

Neutral and organic — whites, creams, soft blush, sage, and an abundance of foliage and texture. A more editorial, less obviously autumnal palette that still feels completely connected to the season.

Bold and dramatic — deep burgundy, oxblood, near-black dahlias, amaranth, and rich foliage. For couples who want their fall wedding flowers to make a genuine statement.

The light in fall at Lake Tahoe

Photographers will tell you this too: the light in September and October at Lake Tahoe is extraordinary. The sun sits lower in the sky, the shadows are longer, and the golden hour, which in summer lasts maybe 30 minutes, stretches across most of the late afternoon.

What that means for your flowers is that the warm, deep tones of fall blooms are lit in a way that makes them glow. Cafe au lait dahlias in late afternoon fall light look like they're lit from within. Burgundy amaranth against an aspen grove turning gold is one of the most beautiful things we get to create all year.

If you're considering fall for your Lake Tahoe wedding, the light alone is reason enough.

Fall Lake Tahoe wedding venues in season

Almost every Lake Tahoe wedding venue is available in fall and many couples find September and October dates easier to secure than peak summer. Edgewood Tahoe, Palisades High Camp, the Hellman-Ehrman Mansion, Valhalla Tahoe, and private estates across the basin are all stunning in fall and in many cases more beautiful than they are in summer because of the foliage and the light.

The Hellman-Ehrman Mansion in particular is extraordinary in fall, the estate grounds are surrounded by trees that turn in October, and the combination of the historic architecture, the lake view, and the autumn foliage creates a setting that doesn't need much from flowers to be magical.

When to book for a fall Lake Tahoe wedding

Fall Lake Tahoe wedding florists, especially those who take one wedding per date, book 12–18 months in advance for September and October dates. The secret is getting out. Couples are increasingly choosing fall for the reasons above, and availability is tightening.

If you're considering a September or October Lake Tahoe wedding, reaching out to your florist now, even if your date is still 12–18 months away is the right move.

We love fall weddings

Golden Flowers is a Lake Tahoe wedding florist based in Incline Village, designing foam-free, seasonally grown Lake Tahoe wedding flowers for couples getting married across the Sierra Nevada. Fall is our favorite season and some of our most beautiful work happens in September and October.

If you're planning a fall Lake Tahoe wedding, we'd love to hear about it.
